clue.text: A fellow to irritate, causing a breach of the peace

parts.note: F is a standard abbreviation for fellow, as in FRS
to fray is to irritate or wear down, as with frayed nerves or tempers

explanation.surface: Someone goads a companion until a public disturbance breaks out.
explanation.definitionFit: An affray is a fight in a public place, a legal term for disturbing public order.

clue.text: Athenian clad in some metal

indicators.note: one piece is dressed in another, so the word for some wraps around the Athenian

parts.note: some means any, as in 'have you any?'
Timon of Athens is the title character of Shakespeare's play, so an Athenian here is TIMON

explanation.surface: A citizen of ancient Athens is dressed in a coat of metal armour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Athenian' is not a general Greek but one famous man: Shakespeare's Timon of Athens.
explanation.definitionFit: Antimony is a brittle silvery chemical element, classed as a metalloid and traditionally listed among the metals.

clue.text: I play a pivotal part in awful, crummy film. -

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of words awful crummy, read across the comma

explanation.surface: An actor confesses to having a key role in a dreadful, cheap film.
explanation.walkthrough: The trailing dots link this clue to 3-down, whose clue begins with dots too; 'film' is just surface padding.
explanation.definitionFit: A fulcrum is the point on which a lever turns, so it literally has the pivotal role.

clue.text: … as I behold crook getting wiped out

indicators.note: crook as an adjective means bent or out of order, so these letters are twisted into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Continuing from 2-down, the speaker watches a criminal being killed off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crook' looks like a noun, a criminal, but it is used as the Australian adjective meaning bad or bent, signalling the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: To abolish something is to do away with it entirely, so it has been eliminated.

clue.text: During fight, there's a need to prevent release of information

definitions.note: a verbal phrase standing for a noun meaning a suppression of news

indicators.note: the need occurs during the fight, so its word goes inside the word for a fight

parts.note: a bout is a boxing or wrestling contest
a lack is a want or need of something

explanation.surface: In the middle of a war, censors must keep news from getting out.
explanation.definitionFit: A news blackout is an official suppression of reports, keeping facts from the public.

clue.text: Flower found in another place

definitions.meaning: a wild plant, the cuckoo-pint or wild arum, has this folk name
MPs in the House of Commons traditionally refer to the House of Lords as 'another place', and peers and peeresses sit there

explanation.surface: A bloom turns up somewhere unexpected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Another place' is the Commons' polite name for the House of Lords, the upper chamber of the UK Parliament, whose members are titled men and women.
explanation.definitionFit: The arum is popularly called by this name, and titled peers of both sexes sit in the upper house.

clue.text: Conceal pain following cold

indicators.note: the pain comes after the cold, so its word is placed second

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
an ache is a dull pain

explanation.surface: Someone hides their suffering after catching a chill.
explanation.definitionFit: To cache something is to hide it away in a secret store.

clue.text: Transatlantic run, we hear

indicators.note: the listeners' report signals that the word for run is only spoken, then spelt another way

parts.note: to oversee is to supervise or run an operation

explanation.surface: An ocean crossing or sprint across the Atlantic, as reported by hearsay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'run' tempts as a race or a journey; it is the verb meaning manage.
explanation.definitionFit: Oversea means abroad, across the ocean, which is what a transatlantic voyage is.

clue.text: Young men and women in the army advanced

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force
to advance money is to lend it, so advanced means lent

explanation.surface: Youngsters serving in the military are promoted.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is the Territorial Army, the UK's part-time reserve; 'in' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Colloquially, the local talent means the attractive young people of an area.

clue.text: Recognition provided I fancied it — not I, strangely

indicators.note: strangely says the letters behave oddly, so the words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone recognises a thing only on the odd condition that it wasn't them who fancied it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'provided' is only a link; the fodder is all fourteen letters of I FANCIED IT NOT I.
explanation.definitionFit: Identification is the act of recognising who or what something is.

clue.text: Communist revolution has worker heartlessly backing unreasonable demand

indicators.note: backing means the whole string of pieces is read in reverse

parts.note: red is the traditional colour and nickname of a communist
a roll is a turn over, one revolution

indicators.note: heartlessly means the middle letter of the worker word is removed

parts.note: an ant is the standard crossword worker, from the worker ant

explanation.surface: A Red uprising involves workers turning against those without compassion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' reverses all of RED + ROLL + AT (ANT less its middle N, from 'heartlessly'), giving TA + LLOR + DER.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall order is a request that is very hard or unrealistic to fulfil.

clue.text: Caught right, fish may be seen here

definitions.text: Caught right, fish may be seen here

parts.note: C is the cricket scoring abbreviation for caught
an eel is a long snake-like fish

explanation.surface: An angler's basket, where a properly landed fish ends up.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer while also building it, an all-in-one.
explanation.definitionFit: A creel is a wicker basket in which anglers keep their catch.

clue.text: Communist girl accepts a kiss

indicators.note: the girl takes in the kiss, so her name holds it inside

parts.note: Marian is a girl's name
X is the kiss written at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: A left-wing young woman agrees to be kissed.
explanation.definitionFit: Marxian means following Karl Marx's doctrines, the basis of communism.

clue.text: Stamps collected by one of the family

definitions.meaning: stamps on, treads down hard, as a two-word phrase
a spouse's son from an earlier marriage is a relative by marriage

explanation.surface: A family member's stamp collection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collected' hints that the two-word phrase meaning stamps is run together as one word; 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A stepson is a husband's or wife's child from a previous partner, so a family relation; to step on is to stamp.

clue.text: Young girl sees city at speed

parts.note: NY is New York
mph, miles per hour, is a measure of speed

explanation.surface: A girl watches the city rush by.
explanation.definitionFit: A nymph is a beautiful young woman, from the maiden spirits of myth.

clue.text: Tavern (foreign) no good for the stomach

parts.note: an inn is a tavern

indicators.note: no good means the letter standing for good is dropped

parts.note: German is one example of a foreign nationality

explanation.surface: A pub abroad that serves bad food for the belly.
explanation.walkthrough: G for good is the dropped letter; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Humorously, the inner man means one's appetite or belly.

clue.text: Reasons to limit the distribution of alcohol

definitions.note: plural noun for a singular noun meaning the set of reasons

parts.note: to ration goods is to restrict how much each person gets
ale is an alcoholic drink, a beer

explanation.surface: Justifications for restricting how much drink is handed out.
explanation.definitionFit: A rationale is the underlying set of grounds for a decision or belief.

clue.text: Occult alms city distributed

indicators.note: distributed means spread around, so these letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Charity handed out in a town with a mysterious air.
explanation.definitionFit: Mystical and occult both describe hidden, supernatural or spiritual matters.

clue.text: One primate exercises another

parts.note: a man is one kind of primate
drill is military exercise or training

explanation.surface: One ape puts another through its paces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' is the definition: another primate, the baboon-like monkey; 'drill' is also a primate, a neat double layer.
explanation.definitionFit: A mandrill is a large West African monkey, so a further member of the primate order.

clue.text: A victory in the Lancers' breakthrough

indicators.note: the victory letter is placed inside the word for the Lancers

parts.note: the Lancers is a quadrille, an old square dance
V is for victory, as in the V-sign

explanation.surface: A cavalry regiment wins a battle and breaks through the lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Lancers' looks like a cavalry regiment, but it is a nineteenth-century square dance.
explanation.definitionFit: An advance is a step forward or a development, as is a breakthrough.

clue.text: Score in match unbelievable and unknown

parts.note: a tall story is one hard to believe
Y is one of the algebraic unknowns, x, y, z

explanation.surface: An incredible scoreline in a game.
explanation.definitionFit: A tally is a running count of points, the score kept during a game.

clue.text: Vessel of less tonnage

definitions.meaning: a flat-bottomed barge used to unload ships

explanation.surface: A ship that weighs less than another.
explanation.definitionFit: A lighter is a barge for ferrying cargo, and the word is also the comparative meaning less heavy.

clue.text: Theme has run in parallel

indicators.note: the theme word has the run letter inside it

parts.note: a topic is a subject or theme
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: The subject has been running alongside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parallel' looks like an adjective but is the noun: a line of latitude.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tropics of Cancer and Capricorn are parallels of latitude either side of the equator.

clue.text: I arrive shattered in resort area

indicators.note: shattered means broken into pieces, so these letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: A traveller turns up exhausted at a holiday resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shattered' reads as British slang for exhausted; it signals the anagram. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Riviera is the Mediterranean coast of France and Italy, famous for its holiday towns.

clue.text: Leaders in England today have ignored Christian principles

definitions.note: plural noun for a singular noun meaning a set of moral standards

indicators.note: leaders are the front letters, taken from each following word

explanation.surface: Modern English leaders are accused of abandoning Christian values.
explanation.definitionFit: An ethic is a body of moral principles, as in the work ethic.

clue.text: Medical man should account for prolonged shortage

parts.note: Dr is the abbreviation for doctor
ought means should

explanation.surface: A doctor ought to explain a long scarcity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'account for' is a link joining the pieces to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A drought is a long spell without rain, and more loosely any lasting scarcity.

clue.text: Horse box

definitions.meaning: a Suffolk ... is a heavy draught horse breed
to box is to hit with the fists

explanation.surface: A trailer for carrying a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a horsebox, a vehicle; the Suffolk Punch is an English farm horse breed.
explanation.definitionFit: The Suffolk Punch is a breed of workhorse, and to box is to strike with blows.

clue.text: Alice isn't exceptionally unyielding

indicators.note: exceptionally means in an unusual way, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Alice is not remarkably stubborn.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inelastic does not stretch or give way under pressure.

clue.text: Row of houses takes a source of capital — notes and coin

indicators.note: a source is where something starts, so the first letter of capital is taken

parts.note: two musical notes from sol-fa, re and s for soh
a cent is a small coin

explanation.surface: A street of homes draws in money, both banknotes and change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes' is a link. In tonic sol-fa, soh is written S, so the notes are RE + S.
explanation.definitionFit: A crescent is a curved street of houses, typical of Georgian British towns such as Bath.

clue.text: Paddy has a lot of character and spirit

parts.note: a paddy is a fit of temper, as is a pet

indicators.note: a lot of means most but not all, so the last letter of the character word is cut

parts.note: a role is a character played by an actor

explanation.surface: An Irishman full of personality and vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paddy' looks like an Irish name but means a tantrum; 'has' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Petrol is called motor spirit, a refined volatile fuel.
